topo.title: Network topology
topo.hint: Line colour = chain · line width = traffic today · pick a chain to isolate it

alerts.title: Needs attention
alerts.sub: {{count}} items · by severity · same source as Telegram alerts

msg.broken: Every member of {{group}} is offline; hop {{hop}} is down
msg.degraded: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{loss}} loss, {{ms}} latency is over the {{threshold}} alert threshold
msg.pending: Config changed and not yet pushed to {{count}} servers

path.title: Path selection
path.hint: Every 15 seconds the path with the lowest total latency to the exit wins; a new path must be clearly faster two rounds in a row before it takes over.

row.memberLatency: Latency from each member to the next group

legend.title: Latency colours:
legend.warn: over the group's alert threshold, or loss ≥ 1%
legend.lan: "via LAN" = this hop uses a private address, as chosen by probing

problem.tooShort: A chain needs an entry group and an exit group, connected by a line
problem.multiEntry: The trunk must be a single line: {{count}} groups have no previous hop
problem.loose: "{{group}}" is not connected to the chain
problem.branchOpen: The branch through "{{group}}" does not merge back into the trunk
problem.pathOpen: The paths leaving "{{group}}" do not meet in the same group

pool.hint: Drag onto the canvas for a new group, or onto a group to join it — a click works too.
pool.hintNodes: Drag a landing node into the exit group: the last hop relays to that node.

empty.title: The canvas is empty
empty.desc: Drag servers in from the pool (or click them), then pull a line from the dot on a group's right edge to the next group. Double-click a line to delete it.

chain.title: Chain settings
chain.hint: Click a group on the canvas to edit it
chain.name: Chain name
chain.ports: Port range (entry ports of the chain's nodes come from here)
chain.engineHint: Used by every group without its own engine. Kernel engines use less CPU; rules they cannot do (rate limits, IPv6, …) fall back to relay automatically.
chain.clientIpHint: The entry prepends a PROXY header, so the exit node sees the client's real IP.
chain.stickyHint: Connections from one client land on the same server at every hop.
chain.domainHint: The master keeps the A / AAAA records in step with the entry group's health; a dead entry server is taken out of DNS.

group.title: Group settings
group.name: Group name
group.strategyHint: Decides how traffic is spread over this group's members; the previous hop carries it out.
group.strategyEntry: An entry group has no previous hop, so no strategy applies.
group.engineHint: Applies only to the hop leaving this group.
group.branchHint: On the canvas, pull a line from the purple dot beside a server to another group: that server takes its own detour and must join the trunk's next hop again.
group.pathPolicy: Lowest latency first: every 15 seconds the path with the lowest total latency to the exit wins.

probe.title: Latency probe
probe.e2e: End-to-end paths (hops added up, {{count}} in total)
probe.handshakeHint: The master does a TLS handshake against the entry of every node on the chain: packets really travel each hop to the landing and back. TLS / Reality nodes only.
probe.needChain: Build the chain first: it needs a connected entry group and exit group.

iperf.title: iperf3 throughput test
iperf.subServers: The receiver starts a one-off server in the chain's port range and closes it afterwards
iperf.subProxy: The initiator temporarily uses the landing node as an outbound and downloads a large file through it
iperf.noteServers: iperf3 is installed automatically when a server lacks it. Test traffic is not billed to any user, but it does use the servers' bandwidth and traffic quota.
iperf.noteProxy: Tests through a node use system credentials and are not billed to any user, but they use the bandwidth and traffic of the initiator and of the landing node's server.

matrix.title: Full-chain speed test
matrix.desc: iperf3 · every entry server → every exit server, over the chain's real forwarding path
matrix.noPairs: This chain has no entry and exit to test yet
matrix.note: The master picks a free port in the chain's port range and pushes a temporary set of forwarding rules used only for the test: the exit starts an iperf3 server, the entry runs the client, and everything is removed afterwards. The temporary rules do not count toward traffic, billing or alerts. Closing this dialog does not interrupt a test.
matrix.landingNote: The exit is a landing node, so the test stops at the last group of forwarding servers.
matrix.empty: Nothing tested yet. Press "Start test" to measure every entry server against every exit server.

heatHint.tcp: Mbps, retransmits in brackets; click a cell to see that pair's curve
heatHint.udp: Mbps, loss in brackets; click a cell to see that pair's curve

matrix.barsHint: · thin pale bars are the run being compared
matrix.curvesHint: · with both directions, entry → exit is drawn
